title: Skybox image and video product evaluation
relevance_reason: The paper is about satellite image and video product evaluation; 'street vector databases' is mentioned only once in passing as a georeferencing tool for videos, with no discussion of vector database technology, indexing, or similarity search.
research_focus: Evaluation of SkySat satellite still image quality, georeferencing accuracy, and video product capabilities, with comparison against Worldview-3 (WV-3) data acquired over the same area.
method: Image quality assessment (radiometric, resolution, signal-to-noise ratio), georeferencing accuracy evaluation using ground control points (GCPs) and RPC-based orthorectification, video analysis for vehicle speed detection and motion-based georeferencing, and digital surface model generation from video, all compared against WV-3 reference data.
application_domain: Remote sensing, satellite imagery evaluation, georeferencing, and video-based geolocation
results_summary: The paper evaluated SkySat still image and video products against WV-3 reference data. Georeferencing of SkySat still imagery required more than 50 GCPs compared to only 2 for WV-3, and direct georeferencing accuracy was in the range of 100 to 200 m. Video analysis demonstrated vehicle speed detection with precision better than 0.8 mph and automatic motion detection for georeferencing to street vector data. Digital surface models generated from video achieved a height accuracy of 1.2 m (NMAD). Overall, image quality was deemed good but radiometric quality was lower than WV-3, and the small footprint limits applications to local high-frequency monitoring.
limitations: Relatively small footprint of video and still imagery products limits applications to local monitoring; Radiometric quality of SkySat data is lower than WV-3 data acquired in similar conditions; Direct georeferencing accuracy is low, in the range of 100 to 200 m; Merged SkySat geo product cannot be adjusted or orthorectified well and is not suitable when precise georeferencing is required; Higher noise level in video products compared to still imagery
research_gaps: Using the physical camera model for image orientation to potentially reduce the number of required GCPs
